findings.location: source.html paragraph 4 (sentence containing “The expression “happy as a lark”...)
findings.source_quote: The expression “happy as a lark” is so common a term that it is used by people who have never even ventured to the meadow to see or hear a lark.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the correct target-language common name for the bird meant by “lark” (skylark) rather than κούκος (cuckoo). Replace ««ευτυχισμένος σαν κούκος»» with a phrase using 'αλκυόνα' is incorrect — use 'αλκυών' only if it's the intended bird in Greek idiom; best is 'ευτυχισμένος σαν αλκυόνα/αλκυών (ή 'σαν τσαλαπετεινός' only if idiom requires).' Prefer: «η έκφραση «ευτυχισμένος σαν αλκυόνα (lark)» ...» or keep the English 'lark' in parentheses if no standard Greek idiom is intended.
findings.translation_quote: Η έκφραση «ευτυχισμένος σαν κούκος» είναι τόσο συνηθισμένος όρος που τη χρησιμοποιούν άνθρωποι που δεν έχουν ποτέ καν τολμήσει να πάνε στο λιβάδι για να δουν ή να ακούσουν έναν κούκο.

findings.location: source.html multiple paragraphs listing bird species (paragraphs 6 and 7 and elsewhere)
findings.source_quote: The robin opens up the choir in early spring, but his song is soon surpassed in beauty by the song sparrow and again by the rose-breasted grosbeak. The song of the wren trumps them all for longevity and vibrancy. The canary sings in a cage, while the nightingale sings in the dark. The robins sing in the rain. The buntings fill in the heat of the day when other birds are silent.
findings.suggested_fix: Either translate the bird names consistently into common Modern Greek names or render the English common names in italics/quotation marks or in parentheses as transliterations. Currently a mix of English names (robin, song sparrow, rose-breasted grosbeak, wren, nightingale, buntings) and English+Greek variants appears. Make the approach consistent and use accurate equivalents if available. Examples: robin → 'σπουργιτότρυγος' is not standard; common Greek choices: 'ερυθρόστικτος (robin) / κόκκινος θηραυγός' — if no concise Greek equivalents are standard, keep the English name in parentheses after a Greek descriptor (e.g., «ο robin (ερυθρόστιχτος)»). Ensure the same convention is used for all bird names throughout the article.
findings.translation_quote: Ο robin ανοίγει την χορωδία νωρίς την άνοιξη, αλλά το άσμα του σύντομα ξεπερνιέται σε ομορφιά από το song sparrow και ξανά από το rose-breasted grosbeak. Το τραγούδι του wren τα υπερτερεί όλα ... Το κανάρι τραγουδά σε κλουβί, ενώ η ναϊνάδα (nightingale) τραγουδά στο σκοτάδι. Οι robins τραγουδούν στη βροχή. Τα buntings γεμίζουν τη ζέστη της ημέρας...

findings.source_quote: Paul pleaded with the Corinthian church, “Doth not nature itself teach you?” … “Is any merry? Let him sing psalms” (James 5:13). … “And he hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God” (Ps 40:3). … On 22 occasions, the Scriptures reiterate the phrase, I will sing.
findings.suggested_fix: The authoritative English article contains quoted Scripture and short quoted phrases in English. In the translation some biblical quotations remain in English while the surrounding text is Greek. This is acceptable if deliberate, but it should be consistent: either keep all quoted Scripture exactly as printed in English (verbatim) or provide a clear, consistent presentation (e.g., Greek translation followed by the printed English in parentheses). Ensure that every Scripture quotation matches the exact printed English in the source (do not substitute alternate wording) or else render the printed English in full. For example, where the source writes “Doth not nature itself teach you?” ensure the same punctuation and wording are preserved if the quote is left in English, or present the English in parentheses after the Greek rendering.
findings.translation_quote: … Ο Παύλος παρακάλεσε την εκκλησία της Κορίνθου, “Doth not nature itself teach you?” … “Is any merry? Let him sing psalms” (James 5:13). … “And he hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God” (Ps 40:3). … Σε 22 περιπτώσεις, οι Γραφές επαναλαμβάνουν τη φράση, I will sing.
